biography: Steijn Schothorst hails from the windswept Dutch coast, a place where the relentless North Sea mirrors the restless spirit within him. Growing up near the Zandvoort circuit, the roar of engines was the soundtrack to his childhood. Unlike the children building sandcastles, Steijn was building miniature race cars from Lego, meticulously studying the racing lines of his local heroes. His father, a former karting enthusiast, recognized his son's burning passion and enrolled him in karting at the age of 8. Steijn quickly outpaced his peers, his aggressive style earning him both wins and reprimands. A defining moment came during the Dutch National Karting Championship when, after a daring last-lap overtake, he secured the title, his father's roaring approval echoing in his ears. Now at 21, Steijn is climbing the ladder in the Formula Trainer Advance series, his raw talent undeniable, but his temperament still a work in progress. He is determined to prove that calculated aggression can lead to victory.
drivingStyle: Steijn's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He attacks corners with a ferocity that often borders on reckless, pushing the car to its absolute limit. He favors late braking and aggressive turn-in, often unsettling the car but somehow managing to maintain control. Tire management is not his forte; he tends to burn through his rubber early in a race, relying on raw pace to build a lead. Under pressure, Steijn can become erratic, prone to mistakes, but also capable of moments of breathtaking brilliance. He thrives on the adrenaline rush of wheel-to-wheel combat, viewing each race as a personal battle against his rivals.

rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities; Isabelle criticizes Steijn's aggressive driving as dangerous, while Steijn dismisses her as 'too cautious'.
They were neck-and-neck in the Formula Trainer Advance championship last season, resulting in several on-track collisions and a heated rivalry for the title.
Marcus is a veteran, known for his defensive skill, who views Steijn as an upstart who needs to 'learn some respect' before getting past him.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, even if they're full of holes.
Listens to a specific Dutch techno song on repeat before every race to get pumped up.
Has a habit of tapping the steering wheel a specific number of times before the start, a ritual passed down from his father.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Dutch National Karting Championship at the age of 16 with a daring last-lap overtake, proving his potential to the world.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final race of the Formula Trainer Advance season last year, costing him the championship title.
